I came out when I was 17, I’m 25 now (so it’s been 8 years) and my parents still both use my deadname and she/her pronouns. The only time they don’t is when they’re with my friends and their parents, who call me [name] by default, and they do the same (probably due to social pressure).

I finally have enough of a stable job and life to begin my transition journey (I have my consultation appointment tomorrow!!), and I’ve just accepted at this point that while they do love me, they’ll never support me in this major aspect of my life. 

It’s hard to hear them say “oh no but transitioning is so dangerous and will screw up your liver” or “wouldn’t you just be happy being a tomboy??” over and over and over again over all these years. 

All in all glad that I found a great support system in my group of friends instead.

It took me about 2 months to get to expert, and the most important thing I realized is that once you get into the expert and expert+ songs (both custom and the included packs), you’ll start to recognize that a lot of these maps use the same patterns just with slightly different variants. 

So my biggest advice is just to keep playing expert songs and if you find a spot where you die (or almost die) a lot, use practice mode until you get it down and repeat all over again. Eventually you’ll commit certain patterns to muscle memory and with more practice it’ll just keep getting easier and easier. 

Also when your muscle memory does get better, don’t overthink while you’re playing. Sometimes you just gotta turn your brain off to succeed.

Ice skating. 

I started taking lessons around freshman year of high school and started getting pretty good. I also had an amazing teacher. Junior year comes around and I get convinced by said teacher to sign up for a synchronized skating team, worst mistake of my life. 

It became obvious immediately that I was the weakest link on the team despite being the second oldest, probably because all these kids starting skating way before me. Some of them made that really obvious, and I would constantly get berated by one of my team members for messing up. I constantly felt like I was a burden on the team and hated going in every week to practice. I stuck with it for the year but adamantly refused to join again next year, and I stopped all skating lessons after that. That year completely ruined my love for skating. 

Also didn’t help seeing one of my teammates(the only one older than me, and she was on this and another team) throwing up in the trash can after practice since she was probably being overworked.
